_meta.purpose: Fixes the architecture nuance permanently. 'I test a RAG chatbot' is the single easiest thing to get wrong about this platform, and it is wrong five times out of six.
_meta.rule: Retrieval-augmented generation is limited to the India Maternal Health program. Nothing on this site may describe the platform, or my work, as RAG in general. The {% architectureNote %} shortcode renders the clarification identically everywhere so it is never paraphrased into something inaccurate.
_meta.disclosure: Programs are named by country and health area only. Sponsoring partners are not named anywhere on this site.

rag.label: RAG retrieval
rag.short: Dense and sparse retrieval fused, then generation grounded in the retrieved passages.
rag.evaluates: Retrieval quality as well as generation quality — context precision, faithfulness, and whether the right passage was found at all.

snippets.label: Smart Snippets with intent classification
snippets.short: An intent classifier routes the utterance, generation draws on curated snippet content, and a vector semantic cache serves repeat questions.
snippets.evaluates: Classification correctness, generation quality against the snippet, and cache correctness. There is no retrieval step to evaluate.

dispatcher.label: Family Planning dispatcher
dispatcher.short: A dispatcher routes to LLM-generated responses within a defined journey graph.
dispatcher.evaluates: Journey routing integrity and response quality. Not retrieval.

programs.note: The only RAG program on the platform, and the only one where retrieval quality is something I can measure. It also carries the highest clinical stakes: a pregnancy-complication symptom described in Assamese has to reach a danger-sign response, not a sympathetic non-answer.

A separate program from India Maternal Health, with a separate architecture and a separately evaluated dataset. Conflating the two India programs into 'the India chatbot' is the most common mistake made about this platform, including in my own earlier writing.
Thai has no word boundaries, which breaks tokenisation assumptions that hold silently in every other language on the platform.
A 32-node journey graph across nine phases with two entry paths — the largest journey configuration on the platform, and the one that motivated structural snapshot validation of the config itself.
programs.confidence: The journey structure I can state precisely because I gated it. I am less certain of the exact generation path here than for the other five, so I do not claim it in detail.

architectureNote.short: Six country programs, three generation architectures. Only India Maternal Health is RAG.
architectureNote.long: The platform runs six country programs across three different generation architectures. Retrieval-augmented generation is used in exactly one of them — India Maternal Health. The three HPV programs use intent classification with curated snippet generation and a semantic cache; the three family planning programs use a dispatcher over a journey graph. This matters for evaluation because you cannot measure context precision on a system that never retrieves anything. Most of the work below is about building one evaluation framework across all three without pretending they are the same system.
